children: TD Cowen on Monday initiated coverage of Space Exploration Technologies Corp.
, better known as SpaceX, with a Buy rating, citing a potentially massive opportunity in artificial intelligence computing alongside continued growth in Starlink and launch services.

terrestrial AI compute-leasing business could become its largest near-term revenue opportunity. TD Cowen estimates AI compute leasing could generate about $14 billion of revenue in 2026, equal to roughly 35% of SpaceX’s
total, before rising to $66 billion in 2027 and $133 billion in 2028.
TD Cowen expects terrestrial AI compute leasing, including services for customers such as xAI and Anthropic, to account for about 60% of SpaceX

revenue in 2027. The analysts led by John Blackledge estimate the business will drive most of the company’s revenue growth through the first quarter of 2027 with the rapid addition of ground-based gigawatt capacity.
Longer term, the analysts see SpaceX

shifting more heavily toward its traditional space businesses. TD Cowen forecasts Starlink, launch services and other space-related operations will become increasingly important as AI compute growth slows from its initial surge. The firm estimates SpaceX
could lease 44% to 49% of its AI compute capacity between 2027 and 2031.

Starlink remains another major growth engine. TD Cowen expects the satellite internet service to dominate broadband markets that are poorly served by terrestrial networks, projecting 107 million consumer subscribers by 2031, including about 10 million in the U.S. The analysts also see enterprise and government connectivity as a potentially more attractive opportunity because of lower customer acquisition and networking costs.

launch capacity could expand dramatically as Starship matures. TD Cowen estimates the company could approach 1,000 low-Earth-orbit launches annually by 2031, up from an estimated 229 gigawatts of capacity in 2031 under its broader space infrastructure model. More than 85% of launches could eventually support SpaceX's own Starlink and orbital data-center operations rather than outside customers.
For investors, TD Cowen's valuation depends heavily on extraordinary growth assumptions. The firm projects SpaceX

revenue rising from about $18.7 billion in 2025 to $40.9 billion in 2026 and $113.2 billion in 2027, with EBITDA climbing from $6.6 billion to $18.9 billion and then $60.8 billion. Its $200 target compares with the report's stated $148.68 share price on Sept. 25, implying roughly 35% upside.
The central investment question is whether SpaceX
can turn AI infrastructure into a huge new business while simultaneously scaling Starlink, Starship and launch capacity at unprecedented rates.
